newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call easy, gilt steady in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call easy, gilt steady in cautious trade.

text.p: Indian call money eased to end Tuesday at 4.25 percent against opening quotes of 4.5-5.0 percent while prices of government securities were steady in light trade, dealers said.
They said call money eased on good fund supply and rates were expected to remain easy through the rest of the week.
"With the reporting Friday coming up on July 4, there should not be much pressure on call money in the next three days," a dealer at a state-run bank said.
Dealers said a repo auction scheduled to be held later on Tuesday was unlikely to have much impact on liquidity.
"The repo rate is not much lower than call is at the moment," said a dealer. "There will not be too much of a response to the auction."
Prices of government securities were steady in thin, cautious trade with major players keeping to the sidelines on rumours of a forthcoming governemnt bond issue, dealers said.
"The market was quiet today as there is increasing speculation that the government will come out with a medium- or long-term bond issue," said a dealer.
"Market players feel that with call money at low levels, the conditions are right for a fresh bond issue," he said.
The interest securities remain in fewer stocks, dealers said.

The 12.59 percent 2004 newly auctioned government stock rose to 100.64 rupees, against the previous close of 100.55 rupees, 11.75 percent 2001 to 100.32 rupees, from 100.23 rupees, while the 10.75 percent 2000 stock dealt at 99.15 rupees, compared to its previous 98.90 rupees, a dealer said.
